title: Kernel quickfire checklist - Luisa
content:
Morning quickfire log - objective: knock out the small things blocking the afternoon rollout.

1) Triage snapshot (09:15)
- p99 spike on 8/16 sequence length window seen on cluster-prod-east-2 around 03:40 UTC.
- Symptoms: sudden queue growth for model:x86-4b-int8, long tail for kv-cache miss paths. No OOM.
- Initial suspects: batcher mis-estimating available slots, cache eviction jitter, or a device-affinity wobble.

2) Quick reproduction plan (local micro-run)
- aim: reproduce p99 in container with 4 worker threads, tiny load generator.
- commands:
  - docker run --rm -e ENV=local -v $(pwd):/w redwood/runtime:dev bash -c "./run_loadgen --model model:x86-4b-int8 --qps 120 --seq-dist small-8,large-16 --dur 600"
  - tail -f /tmp/runtime-metrics.log | grep p99
- hypothesis: with same seq-dist we should see interleaved misses that cause batching fragmentation

3) Experiments to try (fast, rollbackable)
- A: reduce max-batch-size for model:x86-4b-int8 from 32 -> 24 for 30m, watch p99. JIRA-RT-4321 tracks change.
- B: disable prefix caching for 10m for a subset of requests (route flag quick/no-prefix), check if tail flattens.
- C: bump kv-cache size by +20% on one host (dev-only) to rule out eviction churn.

4) Short TODOs (priority order)
- [ ] Kick experiment A on staging (Ishaan) — rollout id: rollout/quick-2026-03-12-A
- [ ] Add extra logging around batcher.slot_estimate (me) — quick patch so we can see estimated vs actual batch occupancy
- [ ] Run reproduce load locally (me + Mina) and capture flamegraphs at 30s intervals
- [ ] Submit lightweight feature-flag for no-prefix route for canary (Mina)
- [ ] If A improves, prepare rollback notes and policy (include cost delta)

5) Micro-root-cause notes (raw thoughts)
- Seen a ~12% deviation in slot_estimate recently after a small optimizer change (PR #980). Might bias batcher to underfill when seq-dist skews.
- Another angle: nvlink contention at 2:00–4:00 UTC due to cross-tenant maintenance windows — ask infra if any jobs overlapped.

6) Metrics to collect (quick additions)
- Add per-model: batch_fill_ratio, slot_estimate_error (abs(est-actual)/actual), kv_cache_evictions/s, device_mem_headroom.
- Short-term dashboard: last 6h heatmap for slot_estimate_error by minute.

7) Communicate
- Ping on #runtime-incidents with short blurb: "Investigating p99 spike for model:x86-4b-int8; running reduce-batch-size experiment A on staging; will post results by 12:30 PT." (I will post after starting experiment)

8) Quick notes to self for later writeup
- If experiment A helps, note the exact p50/p95/p99 deltas and tokens/sec impact. Capture cost per-token before/after.
- If no improvement, attach flamegraphs and kernel stack traces to JIRA and escalate to SRE for host-level checks.

9) Evening followups (if still unresolved)
- Run network microbench (ib-send/recv) across implicated hosts.
- Ask infra to snapshot NVLINK and GPU driver logs between 02:30-04:30 UTC.

10) Misc micro-tasks (10–20m)
- [ ] Clean up /tmp/runtime-traces older than 72h on dev boxes.
- [ ] Drop a comment on PR #987 asking for perf numbers on long-seq variance.
- [ ] Quick tidy of my local perf toolkit scripts to make flamegraph collection idempotent.

Random scratch ideas (unpolished):
- Could we do adaptive max-batch-size that considers recent slot_estimate_error? simple leaky-integrator to damp oscillations. Worth a spike if current experiments don't land.
- Also think about exposing a lightweight sampling endpoint that returns current batch_fill_ratio per model; useful for alerts.

End of quickfire list.
